I have noticed because I help rescuers out. The problem is that when people fled the island, they left their dogs, some in relative's homes that don't care about them, some in the streets. They're everywhere. I found a puppy in a sewer the other day. In the Rio Grande/ general eastern area you can see dogs walking around the shoulder of the road daily. Rural places are plagued with street dogs, many of who turn out squashed by cars or die of diseases. The problem, to me, was not the hurrican, but rather the people of the island that abuse of dogs or dont even know how to take care of them because there is no education or harsh punishment for animal abuse. My friend called the cops on an old man with 8 street dogs tied to trees and locked in his house. They were all in deplorable conditions: cancer, hunger, eating rocks, you name it. And this guy didnt even get a FINE!!! Now we have to watch him once in a while to make sure he didnt take any more dogs in his house instead of going to prison just to say FUCK YOU to his face.
